claims.claim: This cohort reports that running the game above 60 frames per second breaks physics and sound effects.

citations.review_text:
I'll not write about the game, everyone knows it's a cult classic, a beloved entry of an iconic franchise and it still is so go ahead and enjoy the game and soak in its timeless nostalgia.

This is purely a technical review and addresses some of the shortcoming on this "remaster" release. As of March 2026, the game with some minor issues is finally playable and importantly enjoyable. All these suggestions are valid for the other two games as well.

- The stutters still exists but fixed by using -dx12 in the command line as well as using "Car reflections" set to SCREEN. This is a major performance problem because the implementation is broken, just set it to screen and your frames will double. 
- Use Nvidia upscaling, set your resolution higher than your screen and use DLSS Quality (swap using dlss swapper for the latest, v3.10, preset K) for a crystal clear image quality.  Also use classic lightening. 
- LIMIT your frames to 60fps using RTSS ( do not use internal UE limiter, it's bad) because it breaks physics and sounds.
- If you want more perf. or have a weaker GPU, tweak vehicle lights, volumetric clouds, world shadows and distance. IMO, the only settings that is broken is "car reflections", just set it to lowest (screen space).
- KBM users: the game (and the other two) have aggressive auto-centering which is irritating and near impossible to enjoy the game without a controller. Fix: Use ThirteenAG's Fusion Mods for all these 3 games with a small modification ( do NOT disable intro and menu in the mod options (outside of the game), by default they are set to 1, change it to 0 before starting the game, these mess with Rockstar club and autosave and you'll get errors, (Rockstar's cloud saves are also a bit bugged)
- There's some minor bugs like camera jumps when you drive inside a tunnel, or your sprint speed is too fast in Vice City DE, etc. Nothing can be done about these atm. 

That's it, after years of patches, mod fixes and community help it's finally here. Wha…

cohorts.summary: Reviewers with early playtime note visual glitches, frame rate bugs during specific missions, and difficult swimming controls.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience visual glitches involving floating map textures, such as grass floating in the air.

citations.review_text:
Beautiful rework of the game, however, the soundtracks [i](cutsenes, voices, car sounds and etc.)[/i] are low quality. There are a few bugs that I don't like as well, for example [b]diving (swimming)[/b] is not possible, it randomly dives, going down/controlling CJ is impossible on PC/Keyboard [i](should work properly on a controller though)[/i].

The minimap itself is nicer, it tracks the target/mission like in GTA IV/V, marking a blip works too in this manner.

There are some visually dark places which are kind of annoying. Some map textures are just floating around, like grass.

Overall, very nostalgic game, love it, but would rather choose the original version and mod it instead.

The story follows Carl "CJ" Johnson, who returns to Los Santos after his mother's death. Throughout the game, CJ rebuilds his family, fights rival gangs, and uncovers corruption across the state of San Andreas.

My Opinion:

GTA: San Andreas still has one of the best stories in the Grand Theft Auto series.


Graphics – ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ (8.5/10)

The Definitive Edition features:

Improved lighting
Better textures
Higher-resolution models
Longer draw distance
Modern visual effects

Pros

Beautiful lighting
Better reflections
Sharper textures

Cons

Some character models still look odd.
A few visual bugs remain.

I really don't understand why GTA: San Andreas – The Definitive Edition locks the camera, even when I'm just walking or driving. They also removed the high-speed motion blur, and when I play with a controller, it sometimes starts vibrating nonstop for no reason. The only way to fix it is to restart the game. On top of that, the different weather effects don't look nearly as good as they did in the original. Even though this is supposed to be a modernized remaster, I honestly think it looks worse than the original. The original had a much better atmosphere, while this version just feels cheap. I'm really disappointed with these changes.

Rockstar, my suggestion is to restore the cut beta missions and other removed content from San Andreas, remove the frame rate cap, and bring the original GTA: San Andreas back to Steam. I think that's much closer to what players actually want.

claims.claim: Reviewers point out that character models look cartoonish, plastic, or retain weird rigging and facial features.

citations.review_text: San Andreas is a strong contender for the best GTA game. It has by far my favorite map in the game, despite not "Technically" being the biggest or even second biggest GTA map, to me it feels like the biggest. I love how we have a lot of California and part of Nevada all within this map, each location feeling so vastly different to the rest and all full of personality. This game has probably the best gameplay systems out of the series also, the RPG elements add a lot of depth and are an element GTA has yet to replicate in as good a way. There's so much stuff to do in this game its wild, it took me almost 80 hours to complete a 100% playthrough. I just love GTA games that are period pieces, there's a magic to being brought back to the Los Angeles in the early 90s and the game captures the era so well. Everything from the story, to the radio all work together to set the scene perfectly. This game probably has my second favorite soundtrack of the series.  I also think that after the classic lighting update that this game looks absolutely gorgeous, its san andreas in all its glory with the orange los santos, blue san fierro and purple skied LV and Bone County with updated lighting  and textures. Now character models are definitely where the DE still falter as they never got updated, and yes the textures are not up to current industry standards, but in the guise of "keeping the games art style" I think there's plenty that were updated decently, but also a lot that still just look kinda ugly. To me this version is definitely worth it now however as the QOL changes make up for  some of the gameplay aspects that aged poorly and the game looks fairly decent most the time. Honestly though as someone who originally played the DE back in 2021 I don't see how I ever survived 100% playthroughs before the classic lighting, it looks so bland without it.

GTA San Andreas itself is a great game but this is a mediocre remaster. The character models look stupid and make The Elder Scrolls Oblivions character models look like they were sculpted by Michelangelo in comparison. 

There's also weird character rigging issues which means during cutscenes they all move and deform unnaturally. The developers AI upscaled all of the textures which looks like crap and they also screwed up the texture mapping leading to seams and distortions throughout the world.

It's only worth it at half price while using re-texture and radio restoration mods. The addition of checkpointing and modern UX/controls are good additions.

The real definitive edition is emulating the original 2004 PS2 version which is easy to setup, or building your own remaster by modding the original PC version.

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering Unreal Engine 4 fatal error crashes that disrupt gameplay and cause progress loss.

citations.review_text:
The story carried this version of game, the nostalgia. I came to realize that the replayability of this game's edition is 0, compared to the OG that i have finished countless of times. The first thing that came across to my issue was the Audio, some of it are missing, the Loading screen music itself is rare to chime. The NPC's death cries, some are delayed. What i like about the audio of this game is because of the NPC's death cries, and because of this version it was bugged out. The second issue that came across to my journey is the "Melted House" constant melted house it was annoying to see that those houses, or terrains are melted. Third issue is the Vehicle Handling system, they made Flying controls harder i had to configure my flying controls because of the mouse involvement, while in the OG flying with mouse is minimal, here in this version it's almost as mandatory. Last issue, NPC Cars/Traffic glitch, There are no traffic or cars roaming around while im halfway at Las Venturas act. This glitch made the game more empty. It's worse than Cyberpunk 2077. Just NPC's roaming around, no cars, no bikes, no motors. I finished the story and it's still bugged. I forgot to mention the Fatal UE4 crashes. Man this game is unbearable to play, the only thing that made me stay is because of the story and the nostalgia + the achievements. 

Buy at your own risk, yes the discount is a big help. But i'm more interested replaying the OG version of it (Although this version has bugs in it, but it's not as worse as the Remastered) 

Overall - 5.5/10, So many bugs, it is worse than the OG. Though San Andreas will be always my Top 2 GTA, with GTA 4 being Top 1 and GTA 5 as the Top 3.

UE4 Fatal Error renders the game unplayable due to crashes that occur after any save is made, even the auto saves generated by the game itself. The solution is to roll back to a save that works... unless that save also decides to stop working, despite already saving in another slot from your gameplay on that save file.

DON'T EVEN THINK ABOUT BUYING THIS. 40 HOURS WASTED.

GTA San Andreas Definitive Edition is an unfinished technical disaster, and the title "Definitive" is a cruel joke. Visually it's full of glitches, performance is embarrassing for a two-decade-old game, and the sheer number of bugs is absolutely insane. But that isn't even the worst part.

Game-breaking bug that completely ruined the experience:
I spent over 50 hours playing this game "by the book." I did things progressively, completed every single side quest available, collected all the tags in Los Santos, all the oysters, snapshots, horseshoes, and did everything humanly possible to build up toward that sweet 100% completion rate.

After all that time and effort invested, I finally reach Catalina's bank heist mission.

The result? The game is completely broken.

The ATMs are literally INVINCIBLE.

I pumped over 1,000 rounds directly into a single ATM = zero effect.

I threw over 30 satchel charges onto it = still nothing.

I thought I was doing something wrong, so I searched for a fix online. Guess what? It’s a known issue, and the only "solution" discovered by the community is to START A BRAND NEW SAVE FROM 0.

50 hours of collectibles, and side content wiped out because Grove Street Games couldn't be bothered to fix a game-breaking progression bug.

Final Verdict:
Do not buy this garbage. Stick to the original version with mods if you have it. This edition isn't worth a single cent or a single second of your life.

Rating: 1/10 (and that 1 is purely for nostalgia).

If you at least gave us an option to buy original game on market then i would change my mind and say that this game is worth but only on sale but because you removed the original and gave us this version which is one of the worst i cant recommend it, just mod original version with graphics and reshade and go play that this is not worth it

Just finished game. Took me 54.7 hours.
Yes, the remaster still has plenty of bugs that weren't in the original version - but there's noticeably fewer of them now compared to how it was at launch. What really bugged me though was the controls - I don't understand how they managed to screw them up so badly, especially in the helicopter and plane. Had to get used to a new layout after remapping it myself just to make it somewhat playable.
But despite all these issues, I'm genuinely glad I finished it at 100%. San Andreas is one of the first games I ever played, and it's the one that got me hooked on the GTA series in the first place. The atmosphere of Los Santos, San Fierro, and Las Venturas still holds up, and CJ's journey from a guy coming back for his mother's funeral to someone who flips the whole state upside down remains one of the strongest story arcs in the series. The visual upgrades in the Definitive Edition give it a fresh coat of paint without killing the original's charm.
Bugs and all, replaying this game is still a genuine pleasure.

There are two reasons for the downvote:
1. Bugs.
2. Flying is impossibly hard, which was not the case in the original game. 

One of the issues I had was with the vigilante missions: the game crashed when reaching level 12. The solution I found that worked was to use a hunter helicopter. You can find one either in Verdant Meadows after getting gold in all flying school's missions or in the Heli Hell race (appears in Las Venturas' airport; you can simply fly the helicopter to Verdant Meadows' hangar while in the race, and it will stay there afterwards).

citations.review_text: Same nobody asked for this cash-grab remaster, and to make it worse, Rockstar delisted the original versions so scalpers are selling old Steam keys for over $100. Absolute clown show, thanks for nothing Rockstar.
This "definitive edition" is worse than the original game, and Rockstar delisted the original version from Steam because of pure greed.

Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is one of the best games ever made and remains a timeless classic. Even decades later, its story, characters, world, and sense of freedom are still easy to appreciate.

Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this version. The Definitive Edition was outsourced rather than developed directly by Rockstar, and it feels like the developers were under significant pressure to release it before it was ready. To this day, the game still suffers from technical issues and performance problems that should not exist in a remaster of a classic title.

What makes the situation even more disappointing is that Rockstar delisted the original versions while also taking legal action against modders who had created their own remasters that many fans considered superior.

If you absolutely insist on playing this version, wait for a deep sale. Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas deserves your time, but this Definitive Edition does not deserve full price.

citations.review_text: I've lost count of the number of bugs and glitches. And, as usual, there are no user tracks in the game!

The greatest and most entertaining video game ever made.
Even after almost 2 decades, you can't get enough of this game
There are a few bugs  in the game, but what game doesn't have them? A must-have for everyone!

Even in 2026, after the Definitive Edition was finally 'fixed', this version of San Andreas is a massive pile of bugs and glitches that didn't exist in the OG version of the game. 

The Definitive Edition versions of GTA III and Vice City are largely fine at this point. But San Andreas is still ABSURDLY buggy. Like constantly. Nothing game-breaking. But tons of bugs and glitches happening constantly. I don't think I can go 3 straight minutes without noticing something in the game acting buggy. 

Pedestrians constantly freaking out for absolutely no reason (screaming and running in a panic when nothing is going on around them). This happens regularly.

Jetpack audio not working most of the time. 

Helicopters spawning in car parking spots (including UNDERGROUND GARAGES - yes, a helicopter parked in a car's parking space in an underground car park where it's literally impossible to get a helicopter in or out).

Random instances of texture Z-fighting in certain parts of the map. 

A body of water in Las Venturas that has TWO separate water textures right next to each other with a very clear line of separation between them.

The Mount Chilliad BMX challenge is basically broken, because the spawn location for the bike bugs out after you complete the first BMX race. It will never again spawn where it's supposed to spawn. Most players think the BMX bike stops spawning in completely. As a result, they think the BMX challenges are broken and impossible to complete. 

Here's a little hint: After I completed the first BMX race, I found the bike lying on its side on a random part of the mountain. And it was making noise as if its wheels were spinning fast, despite lying motionless on its side. So I got onto the bike and rode it up to the top of the mountain. I parked the bike where it should be parked. Dismounted and then got back on. Then the next BMX race was triggered. This worked.

There's a good deal of Definitive Edition players who think San Andreas is busted and impossi…

This game in one of my all time favorites and a big part of my childhood. It's easily one of the best GTA titles ever made.
However, the remaster version has some bugs.

San Andreas has always been my favorite in the series and if anything I would always highly suggest anyone who hasn't played to play and now unfortunately without being able to own the original on Steam I still think it's fantastic to get the Definitive Edition and experience it and with only a few minor issues like occasional world clipping... Overall, I think it’s a great way to relive the original experience.
